summary: Ferdinand de Saussure worked in linguistics and Indology. He earned his PhD at Leipzig University and also studied in Geneva, Berlin, and Paris. He taught at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, University of Paris, and University of Geneva.
Ferdinand von Eckstein worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Friedrich Creuzer and served as a member of the Société Asiatique from circa 1823 to 1861.
Fernando Jose Benetti is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Nalanda University and under doctoral supervisor Aleksandra Wenta.

Fernando Tola worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy after studying at the National University of San Marcos. He held posts at the University of Buenos Aires and served as director of the Fundación Instituto de Estudios Budistas.
Fifth Karma Kuchen is active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Penor Rinpoche and succeeded him in 2000.
Filippo De Filippi worked in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at the University of Bologna from circa 1894 to 1903 and at the University of Genoa.

Filippo Marsili specializes in Sinology, history, and archaeology. He completed graduate studies at the University of California, Berkeley, studying under Patricia Berger, Corrado Pensa, and Arcangela Santoro, and held a post at Saint Louis University.

Finnian M. M. Gerety is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned a doctorate at Harvard University in 2015. He completed a postdoctoral fellowship at Yale University (2017–2018) and taught at Brown University.
Fiona Ross works in Indology and linguistics. She studied at SOAS University of London and later held posts at the University of Reading and Tiro Typeworks.

Fitzedward Hall was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute and Harvard. He taught at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, Sanskrit College, and King's College London, and served as librarian at the India Office.

Flavio A. Geisshuesler works in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Lausanne, Bern, and the University of Virginia (PhD 2019 under David Germano), and completed a postdoctoral post at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem in 2019.
Flora Blanchon studied under Léon Vandermeersch and Nicole Vandier-Nicolas, and she taught Jacques Giès.

Florin Deleanu works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a PhD from the University of Hamburg and held professorships at Kansai Medical University and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, among other posts.
Florinda De Simini is an Indologist who held posts at the University of Naples Federico II (attested 2016) and the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (circa 2018).
Francesca Fremantle specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at SOAS University of London from circa 1966 to 1971 and under Chögyam Trungpa from circa 1971 to 1987.

Francesco Sferra works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied under Raffaele Torella and has held posts at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and the University of Naples Federico II.
Francis Brinkley, a scholar in Japanology, studied at the Royal School Dungannon. He later held a post at the University of Tokyo from circa 1878 to 1881.

Francis Buchanan-Hamilton was a physician and researcher in history and archaeology who earned an MD at the University of Edinburgh. He served in the Bengal and Indian Medical Services and directed the Indian Botanic Garden.

Francis Gladwin was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and history. He was a founding member of The Asiatic Society and served as a professor of Persian at Fort William College.

Francis H. Cook was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Wisconsin–Madison. He served as a professor of religious studies at the University of California, Riverside, and later chaired the Numata Center.
